raw_response:
I’ve farmed these nine mu for fifty years, and after agricultural college I spent two decades trying to convince extension stations to listen to farmers instead of the other way around. Now it’s just my wife and me—both seventy—so every kilogram I lift and every yuan I spend has to answer to these bones. I don’t optimize; I survive, and I’ve learned that the cheapest way to lose money is to try to save it at the wrong moment.

My six mu of winter wheat is already in the ground—Jimai 22, sown at 13 kg/mu last October with a base dressing of compound fertilizer. The stand looks adequate, around the right ear-bearing stem density. At booting stage now, I’ll topdress 5 kg urea per mu at heading. My records show that withholding nitrogen at flag-leaf stage costs 8–10 % yield, and at current grain prices that is a false economy I cannot afford. I will irrigate twice more: once at heading if the topsoil dries, and a critical one at grain-filling in mid-May. Pumping costs 40 yuan per mu now, so I’m done with generosity after that. I’ll scout for rust before spraying fungicide; if I don’t see it, I keep the 20 yuan per mu. Target is 460 kg/mu.

The same six mu flips to summer maize immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I hire the village cooperative’s no-till planter—45 yuan per mu, finished in half a day because the turnaround window is brutally tight. I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid at 2.5 kg/mu. I band 50 kg/mu of compound fertilizer at planting, then side-dress 12 kg urea at the seven-leaf stage, bringing total N to about 18 kg/mu. Any more and the August storms lodge the stalks; I learned that in 2012. Two irrigations: one after planting for emergence, and the non-negotiable one at silking in late July. One herbicide application, and I watch for armyworm.

My three mu of cotton is where the cash comes from, but it is also where the cash goes. Cotton hates compaction, so I deep-plow every April. I plant a Bt hybrid at 1.8 kg/mu. Base fertilizer is 40 kg compound per mu, then 15 kg urea at first flowering—about 16 kg N/mu total. I irrigate twice: at squaring and peak bloom. The real expense is pesticide. Even with Bt, aphids and spider mites arrive like clockwork, so I budget four sprays, rotating chemistry to keep resistance down. Picking is manual. My wife and I will handle most of it, but I’ll hire three days of neighborhood help for the peak in September. Target is 280 kg lint per mu, though I never count the lint until the gin pays me.

Total cash outlay this season is about 4,200 yuan. That is tight on a pension and nine mu, but under-investing in the wheat flag-leaf stage or the maize silking irrigation is how a mediocre year becomes a disaster. I keep a small reserve for doctor visits, because at seventy, a bad fall is a bigger risk than a dry July.
